newsitem.title: USA: Intel invests $14.75 million in Avid.
newsitem.headline: Intel invests $14.75 million in Avid.

text.p: Aiming to bring entertainment from the silver screen to the personal computer screen, semiconductor maker Intel Corp. said Monday it invested $14.75 million in video and audio production equipment supplier Avid Technologies Inc.
Tewksbury, Mass.-based Avid has been challenged by the shift in the entertainment market away from traditional platforms such as Apple Computer Inc.'s Macintosh systems.
And Intel took a broad swipe at struggling Apple in signing up Avid -- whose video editing systems were initially based around the Macintosh -- to develop for Intel PCs.
Intel and Avid said in a joint news conference here that the investment was part of an alliance supporting Avid's plans to offer video and audio editing products on the Intel architecture.
The investment, in which Intel will purchase 1,552,632 newly issued shares of Avid at $9.50 a share based on the stock's Friday close. On Monday Avid stock jumped $2 to $11.50.
The deal, unveiled at Intel's "platforms for visual computing" conference here, is part of Intel's effort to launch itself into the world of Hollywood entertainment.

Craig Barrett, Intel's chief operating officer and president-elect, said the company expects machines equipped with its processors to be used for authoring as well as playing multimedia content in coming years.

William Miller, chairman and chief executive of Avid, said he anticipated this will extend beyond Hollywood, to businesses and eventually home users, who could, for example, post video recordings of a child's birthday party on the Internet for family to see.

"We intend to aggressively expand our capabilities on the Intel architecture," Miller said, adding the company will expand its distribution capabilities aimed at the use of Intel-based personal computers.
